The push to save Gaza's fragile truce went into overdrive this weekend.

Trump's envoys — Jared Kushner and Nickolay Mladenov among them — met Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators in Cairo, with Hamas officials in the building, and they're due to sit down with Netanyahu today.

Meanwhile the war in Ukraine had another savage night.

Russian barrages killed at least seven and wounded more than fifty, hitting Kyiv and a major steel plant and torching one of the capital's beloved book markets.

It spilled over the border too — NATO had to shoot down a drone that strayed into Romanian airspace, a nervy reminder of how easily this widens.

Your science note is a rare good-news one from cardiology.

A dirt-cheap, centuries-old heart drug — digoxin, under ten cents a day — turns out to cut hospital stays for heart-failure patients by about a quarter, according to a fresh analysis pooling a big new trial with older ones.

Not a cure, but proof that sometimes the old, near-free medicine still earns its keep.
